source_text: Collegit itaque Apostolus argumentum hoc modo: Si nulli essent haeredes benedictionis, nisi qui ex lege sunt, ut praeputium constabat exclusum, ita consequens erat neminem, qui fuisset ex lege, benedictione privari, id est, si circumcisio tantum valeret, ut sine ea fides nihil valeret, sicut gentes liquebat repulsas, ita probabatur de Iudaeis ad perditionem numquam quisquam ire potuisse.
pass_a_gloss: The Apostle therefore collected an argument in this way: If none were heirs of blessing except those who are from the law, as the foreskin stood excluded, so it was consequent that no one who had been from the law would be deprived of blessing, that is, if circumcision availed so much that without it faith availed nothing, as the nations were clear as having been repulsed, so it was proved that from the Jews no one could ever have gone unto perdition.
pass_b_english: The apostle accordingly formed his argument in this way: if none were heirs of the blessing except those who are of the law, then just as the uncircumcised would clearly be excluded, it would follow that no one who was of the law could be deprived of the blessing. In other words, if circumcision had such power that faith was powerless without it, then just as the Gentiles were clearly rejected, it would be proved that no Jew could ever have gone to destruction (compare Romans 4:14) (Romans 4:14).

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
